title: Agent installers and session bootstrap
objective: workctx can detect Codex, Claude Code, and Gemini CLI, generate project-scoped instruction and skill adapters from canonical sources with drift-detecting manifests, report status, repair and uninstall safely, and open a context in a selected agent — all as typed APIs, without touching user credentials.
business_value: Agent interoperability is a Phase 1 definition-of-done pillar: one canonical rule set serving three agent clients without duplication or drift (risks R-005).
scope: Implement src/workctx/adapters/agents/: client detection (executables on PATH plus client-native project markers) for codex, claude, and gemini with a typed capability report

Adapter generation from canonical sources per doc-13 and the WP-130 manifest spec (docs/reference/skill-adapters.md + schemas/skill-adapter-manifest.schema.json): generate project-scoped skill copies and instruction bridges into client-native locations (.claude/skills/, .gemini/, .codex/ per the adapter strategy), writing the manifest with canonical sha256 hashes and adapter version
Idempotent install: rerunning produces no changes when sources are unchanged; user-owned files are backed up before modification and never deleted on uninstall
status/repair/uninstall APIs: status reports drift by comparing manifest hashes to canonical sources; repair regenerates only stale files; uninstall removes only manifest-listed generated files

Session bootstrap: an open_context API that launches the selected detected client in a context root (subprocess spawn, no credential handling); failure when the client is missing is a clear unavailable-dependency error

Respect the registry: generated adapters record the skill side-effect classes from .agents/skills/registry.yaml as advisory metadata where the client format allows comments/frontmatter the canonical contract permits
Document the adapter strategy per client in docs/reference/agent-adapters.md

D-026: extend the manifest schema (explicit grant) with a per-entry mode — generated (existing) or native-verified (canonical path + hash, no generated file) — with ADR 0008 positive/negative fixtures; Codex uses native-verified entries for skills it reads directly from .agents/skills, generating only what its native behavior actually requires

D-027: create the packaged agent kit (src/workctx/resources/agent_kit/: canonical skills, registry.yaml, bridge templates) with a deterministic sync script (scripts/sync_agent_kit.py) and a byte-equality test against .agents/ sources (D-011 pattern); the installer reads repo .agents/ when present, else the packaged kit
D-028: missing bridges in target projects are generated from packaged templates as manifest-recorded entries; existing user bridges are NEVER modified — status reports divergence instead
D-029: Gemini uses .gemini/ with the native form you select and document; client-version probing against a declared supported-range table, failing safely on unsupported versions
D-030: backups live in project-local .workctx/backups/<timestamp>/, manifest-listed, retained until uninstall
non_goals: No MCP configuration generation — that portion is explicitly deferred until WP-330 defines the server identity (D-014); ship the seam (manifest field reserved) and a NOT-IMPLEMENTED status entry
No CLI wiring (lead wires agent detect/install/status/open after integration)
No changes to canonical skills or the frontmatter schema; the manifest schema is amendable ONLY per the D-026 grant with fixtures
No credential reading, storage, or configuration of any kind (hard security boundary)
deliverables: Agents adapter package: detect, generate, status, repair, uninstall, open — with manifest-driven drift detection and tests in isolated fake home/project directories
acceptance_criteria: Detection reports each client independently using fake executable discovery (no real client required in tests)
Install generates adapters plus a manifest validating against schemas/skill-adapter-manifest.schema.json; hashes match canonical sources
Editing a canonical skill flips status to stale for exactly the affected files (doc-13 acceptance scenario 3); repair regenerates only those; reinstall is a no-op when clean
Uninstall removes only manifest-listed files; a user-created file in the same directory survives; backups exist for any modified user file
Installing for one client never requires or touches another client's directories (doc-13 scenario 1)
No code path reads or writes credentials, tokens, or user-global auth config (negative test greps generated output and API surface)
open_context spawns the selected detected client (subprocess mocked in tests) and fails clearly when missing
security_constraints: Never read, copy, or reference agent authentication credentials or user-global auth files
Generated files stay scoped to the selected project/context; fictional fixtures only
stop_conditions: A gap in the WP-130 manifest spec that requires changing its schema (coordination request)
Any needed change to frozen files, canonical skills, bridges (CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md/AGENTS.md), or pyproject.toml
A client's native format requiring non-portable canonical-skill changes
